items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Well, at the time, I was listening to a whole lot of music -- records -- almost in every neighborhood they had little penny vendors, little restaurants, you walked past, and you could hear all the music you want. Basie, Benny Goodman, Slam Stewart, Slim and Slam ... oh my God, so many good musicians

ctx.x: Well, like I said, I would learn all the while -- I am still learning -- but during those times, the musicians who were around, they would help you. You know. Like, I said this Martha Davis -- when I first started playing with her, she would tell me, she would say, "All right, you're playing in B flat now, and you're playing in E flat, you're playing in D flat, playing in A flat." Well, I knew F,G and C. I knew those keys on my bass. But that was just a beginning. Buster would help me though.

Well, at the time, I was listening to a whole lot of music -- records -- almost in every neighborhood they had little penny vendors, little restaurants, you walked past, and you could hear all the music you want. Basie, Benny Goodman, Slam Stewart, Slim and Slam ... oh my God, so many good musicians -- naturally Duke was at the top.
